title: Urgent customer-impact analysis and targeted patch for hosted inference failures
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary: Multiple high-priority customers reported intermittent 5xx errors, elevated request latencies, and apparent retry storms when calling the Hosted API between 2025-02-16 and 2025-02-18. This ticket is the engineering-led investigation, immediate mitigation, and tracked code patch rollout to resolve the regressions and restore SLOs for affected tenants.

What happened:
- Symptoms: sudden spike in 5xx responses (primarily 503/504), rising tail latency, and increased client-side retries. Some customers experienced persistent failures for specific model routes and longer prompt sizes.
- Scope: ~6 paid tenants with high request rates; internal synthetic load showed a small probability of similar failure modes.
- Initial impact: elevated error budget burn and an on-call escalation from Support to SRE and Inference Platform team.

Timeline (condensed):
- 2025-02-16 02:10 UTC: First customer alert (Support case #C-1142) reporting repeated 503s.
- 2025-02-16 02:22 UTC: SRE paged, triage started. Temporary rate-limits adjusted for the affected tenants to reduce retry amplification.
- 2025-02-16 04:15 UTC: Initial dashboards pointed to request queueing on a subset of serving nodes and higher-than-usual KV cache eviction rates.
- 2025-02-17 09:30 UTC: Repro locally with synthetic load hitting long-context model endpoints; observed a lock contention pattern in the kernel scheduler and degraded async IO responsiveness under specific sequence length distributions.
- 2025-02-18 16:00 UTC: Patch drafted to introduce cooperative backpressure in the request router and a fast-path for short-circuiting retries for transient downstream failures.

Root cause hypothesis (validated by traces and flame graphs):
- Under certain traffic shapes (high concurrency of long-context requests), the runtime's kernel selector and KV cache manager create hotspots where CPU-bound kernel dispatch competes with async IO threads. This causes intermittent request processing stalls, timeouts at the edge proxy, and then client retries which amplify load and push additional nodes over the same contention points.
- The backoff/retry policy combined with the existing retry-unaware routing allowed concurrent retries to overwhelm nodes that had degraded but not fully failed, producing cascading 503/504 responses.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Per-tenant temporary inbound concurrency cap and adjustable retry headers injected at the edge to prevent retry amplification for escalated customers.
- Emergency circuit-breaker thresholds lowered for affected routes to fast-fail and shift traffic to compatible model variants/regions.
- Hotfix (runtime): added a short cooperative yield in the scheduler loop when KV cache eviction rate exceeds a threshold to give async IO threads a chance to progress.

Patch details:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/14862 (runtime: scheduler backpressure yield + retry short-circuit)
- Files changed: scheduler/dispatcher.cpp, kvcache/evictor.go, router/retry_policy.go
- Tests: added stress test harness in infra/tests/stress/scheduler_contention_test.go and unit tests for the retry short-circuit logic.
- Rollout plan: staged deploy to a canary pool (10% capacity) -> monitor for 24 hours -> progressive rollout if stable.

Customer communication and remediation: 
- Sent interim status updates to the 6 escalated accounts with temporary mitigation instructions and ETA for patch rollout.
- Support playbook updated with guidance to set retry headers and enable per-route circuit-breakers while the fix deploys.

Open tasks / next actions:
- [ ] Complete code review and merge PR 14862 (owner: Marcus Lee).
- [ ] Run controlled canary with A/B telemetry capturing queue depth, KV eviction rate, and 95/99 latency for 48 hours.
- [ ] Validate that retry amplification is eliminated under synthetic replay of customer traffic shapes.
- [ ] Follow-up: evaluate longer-term changes to kernel selection heuristics and non-blocking KV eviction (tracked under project Runtime Resilience).
- [ ] Postmortem draft and SLO crediting plan for affected customers (owner: Priya Nair).

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Patch merged and rolled out to production with zero regressions in unrelated routes.
- Confirmed reduction in customer-impacted 5xxs to baseline and SLO in the following 7 days.
- Postmortem published with root cause, timeline, and at least two concrete preventative tasks scheduled into roadmap.
